votes.evidence: A current production caller can supply an unrelated PR URL; this does not require a future integration. /tmp/frozen-75215/products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1101-1118 exposes set_output to task:write callers with task control. Its JSON output is persisted at /tmp/frozen-75215/products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2139-2154. The only protected output key is pr_merged (:1770), and _apply_caller_output explicitly allows changing pr_url (:1778-1787). For a non-internal signal-report run whose acting reviewer opted in, /tmp/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:92-114,126-138 forwards that caller-written URL together with the original task/report IDs. /tmp/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1130-1174 resolves the URL's configured repository and checks only open state and a nonempty head; :1176-1181 and :1223-1229 stamp inbox provenance without verifying bot identity or that the task created the PR. /tmp/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451 converts it into the self-driving flag, which bypasses the bot refusal in /tmp/frozen-75215/tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321-326 and the draft prerequisite in /tmp/frozen-75215/tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:590-591. An unrelated draft, including an external author's PR in a connected repository, therefore enters the approval path under false trusted provenance.
votes.refutation: I first tried to refute the finding by establishing that the receiver was the sole caller and that signal implementations force bot authorship. That is insufficient: the receiver reads output.pr_url, which the existing set_output API lets a task controller replace independently of PR creation. Task access and the review opt-in constrain who can trigger this, but neither attests the selected PR's origin. The webhook re-review path has explicit bot and repository-native checks (/tmp/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-178); the initial task does not call them. Its current-head dedupe only suppresses already reviewed heads and does not reject a fresh unrelated target. The attempted refutation fails on this concrete existing input path.

votes.evidence: There is an existing caller-controlled path, not merely a future integration. products/tasks/backend/presentation/serializers.py:179 accepts arbitrary run output; presentation/views/api.py:1082-1087 exposes PATCH through the task-control gate. visibility.py:22-24,30-46 permits team members to control SIGNAL_REPORT tasks. facade/api.py:2038-2044 merges caller output and :2074-2075 saves it; _apply_caller_output at :1770-1788 protects only pr_merged, explicitly allowing pr_url to change. Therefore a team member with task:write can point a noninternal signal run at an unrelated open draft PR in a configured repository. products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:92-105,111-138 checks the run's report and opt-in, then forwards that URL. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1159-1181 checks only fetched open state and head SHA before stamping the supplied provenance, which :1223-1229 persists. temporal/activities.py:451 enables the engine exception from that stamp; review_local.py:321-330 and review_pr.py:590 relax bot/draft gates without independently verifying the target. This elevates writable task output into trusted approval provenance for an unrelated PR.
votes.refutation: I first checked whether trusted callers and existing linkage guards made the missing validation redundant. The re-review webhook guard requires bot authorship and tasks-facade linkage (tasks.py:169-207), and initial-task tests cover disabled/unsynced/wrong-repository configs (test_tasks.py:947-970). Those do not validate the initial target. The public run-update path accepts replacement pr_url values, and the only attested output key is pr_merged; task access restricts this to authorized team members but does not establish GitHub PR provenance. Existing receiver tests at products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:324-340 merely forward the URL from output. The same team's synced repository and reviewer opt-in limit the blast radius, but do not refute the reachable trust-boundary bypass.

votes.evidence: products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:84-99 promises verified task linkage before the trusted provenance flag is granted. The existing production input violates that promise without any future integration: products/tasks/backend/presentation/serializers.py:179 accepts arbitrary output JSON, views/api.py:1082-1087 forwards an authorized PATCH, and facade/api.py:2038-2044,2075 persists pr_url; its attested-key filter at :1770-1788 protects pr_merged only. An unrelated human-authored draft in the configured repository can consequently receive review and, on an APPROVE verdict, an approval through temporal/activities.py:723-745.
votes.refutation: I first checked whether the internal facade's caller already makes the missing durable-task checks redundant. The receiver does establish a real non-internal signal task and an opted-in reviewer, and the webhook re-review path at tasks.py:167-200 checks bot authorship, native head repository, and tasks-facade linkage. However, the receiver takes the target directly from caller-writable TaskRun.output.pr_url and performs none of those PR checks; the initial task does not invoke the verified webhook helper. The authenticated PATCH is a concrete current production path for that unverified target, so this is more than a documentation discrepancy or a hypothetical future caller.
